world.title: Wildlife populations have declined 73% since 1970-but many of the world's animals still aren't being counted
world.summary: Wildlife populations globally have declined by an average of 73% since 1970, according to the WWF's 2026 Living Planet Index. This index, updated biennially, assesses the changing state of nature. The figure reflects the average decrease in monitored wildlife populations, not a total disappearance of 73% of all animals. Many species remain uncounted in these assessments.

world.title: Boat disaster off Djibouti leaves at least 139 dead, with toll feared to rise
world.summary: At least 139 people, including children, have died after a boat carrying over 300 migrants capsized off the coast of Djibouti, according to the International Organization for Migration. The incident occurred in east Africa, and the death toll is expected to rise. The organization reported that the number only includes those buried by authorities so far.

technology.title: On Air 2026 puts students in charge of global broadcast
technology.summary: On Air 2026 will empower students to manage five live broadcast channels from the University of Westminster, with 150 students in London and an anticipated 1,500 globally. The initiative focuses on skills-led production across various programming categories, including Culture, News, Sport, Film, and Kids. This expansion highlights the growing role of students in international media production.

sports.title: ‘Virat was a bit bitter’: Former India cricketer drops big verdict on Kohli's Test retirement
sports.summary: Former India cricketer Wasim Jaffer commented on Virat Kohli's unexpected retirement from Test cricket, suggesting that Kohli felt bitterness regarding the circumstances of his departure. Jaffer believes that Kohli had the potential to continue playing longer but was dissatisfied with how his exit was managed. This perspective highlights the emotional aspect of Kohli's decision to retire from the format.

sports.title: Inside Lewis Hamilton's Singapore strategy call that helped put Kimi Antonelli in reach of the 2026 title

He expressed regret over the outcome, which not only affected his race but also had implications for Kimi Antonelli's pursuit of the 2026 title. Hamilton's decision ultimately led to his disappointing performance.

health.title: Heart has its reasons
health.summary: At least 25% of Americans experience dyslipidemia, characterized by high cholesterol or fatty acids in the bloodstream. Uncontrolled cholesterol levels elevate the risk of atherosclerotic cardiovascular disease (ASCVD), which involves plaque buildup in blood vessels. This condition can obstruct blood flow to vital organs, potentially leading to serious health issues such as heart attacks and strokes.

health.title: Study finds rare ECHS1 deficiency affects liver and brain
health.summary: A recent study on ECHS1 deficiency, a rare genetic disorder, reveals its impact on both the liver and brain, contributing to epilepsy symptoms. This finding suggests that liver function may influence neurological conditions, prompting a reevaluation of treatment approaches. The research highlights the importance of considering both organs in understanding and managing this genetic epilepsy disorder.

science.title: Mercury’s Greatest Eastern Elongation 2026: What will happen to the night sky on October 12? Check peak time, locations and visibility
science.summary: On October 12, 2026, Mercury will reach its greatest eastern elongation, appearing approximately 25 degrees east of the Sun. This celestial event will be more favorable for observers in the Southern Hemisphere, who will have better visibility. In contrast, skywatchers in India may struggle to see the planet due to its position in the night sky.

science.title: Researchers developed tattoo inks that can be switched on with ultraviolet light and made to disappear in sunlight; tests found the colours remained switchable in skin for up to 2.2 years, opening pos
science.summary: Researchers have developed tattoo inks that can be activated by ultraviolet light and made to disappear in sunlight. Tests indicate these colors remained switchable in skin for up to 2.2 years. The team aims to introduce more colors and lower production costs as the technology evolves, while addressing concerns regarding long-term safety, performance, and practical applications.

science.title: These Chinese coastal cities might be flooded by 2100
science.summary: International scientists predict that coastal cities in China, including Hong Kong and Shanghai, may experience sea level rises of 15 to 20 percent above the global average by 2100, primarily due to melting Antarctic ice. Lin Yucheng, an assistant professor at City University of Hong Kong, emphasized that even limiting warming to 1.5 degrees Celsius may not prevent this outcome.
